definition: The finding that both light and matter show wave behaviour, such as diffraction, in some experiments and particle behaviour, such as the photoelectric effect or Compton scattering, in others.
The wavelength of a moving particle, $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$, where $h$ is the Planck constant and $p$ is the particle's momentum.

The scattering of an X-ray or gamma-ray photon by a free electron, in which the photon gives some energy and momentum to the electron and so leaves with a longer wavelength; it is evidence that photons carry momentum.
